## [Protected storage, crash/private-discovery tests, capability gates and peer preference](ROADMAP.md#protected-storage-crashprivate-discovery-tests-capability-gates-and-peer-preference) `@templartorrent.milestone.safety-and-peer-policy/1`

### Open payload files handle-relative with O_NOFOLLOW at every level

`proposed` · `@templartorrent.work.handle-relative-store/1` · part of `@templartorrent.milestone.safety-and-peer-policy/1`

Close the FileStore hardening gap of DESIGN.md section 3: payload files were probed with symlink_metadata and then created or opened by path, leaving a window in which a symlink planted between the check and the open would be followed. Open every directory component from its parent's descriptor with O_NOFOLLOW | O_DIRECTORY (creating it with mkdirat when absent) and the file with openat O_RDWR | O_CREAT | O_NOFOLLOW on that descriptor, then confirm by fstat that the handle is a regular file. Reads, writes and the resume identity continue to use the handles, never paths. Windows reparse handling stays optional and out of scope.
